question: Why has the lord of the twice-born fallen into Sarasvati amid pearl-splendor?
premises: The lord of the twice-born has fallen.
It occurs in the splendor of pearls.
inference: The moon's descent is poetically described as falling into the river amid pearl-like radiance.
uncertainties: 'dvija+patiḥ' may refer to the moon or another lord; context is needed.
plain_english: Because the lord of the twice-born has fallen into Sarasvati, in the splendor of pearls.
